objective: Make the root judge more kinds of verdicts on compact evidence while specialists keep the heavy work: an evidence-judging skill, a firm visual-judging trigger, Sonnet for artifact review, and design-option and root-cause rules.
scope: Root instruction sections in packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/root/ (skills.md, assignments.md, routing.md and the like), skills under packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/skills/, the route table and agent definitions (find where Reviewer.artifact's model and effort are set, e.g. packages/runtime/src or packages/integrations/claude/src/agents.ts), the tests that pin them, docs/decisions.md, docs/components.md and docs/usage.md where they list skills or routes
constraints: Maintainer's decisions (binding): the root stays the judge and delegates all heavy work; judging reads compact evidence (a reproduction, trace, quoted source, screenshot verdict, diff summary) produced by specialists, never raw logs or whole files, so tokens shift onto the smaller specialist models.

(1) New skill evidence-judging (description starts with the situation: 'Use when a specialist report carries a verdict the root must accept or reject: a blocking review finding, a research claim with conflicting sources or numbers, prose written for people, or a material design choice.'): findings triage: a blocking finding starts a repair only with a reproduction or source-to-sink trace from the reviewer; an unproven one goes back to the same reviewer for evidence (reviewers still do the heavy lifting); research: the root picks the authoritative source, keeps inference labeled, and has a specialist re-derive any number before it is published or decided on; prose for people (user docs, README, PR text, explanatory pages): reviewed by Reviewer.artifact, the root judges the excerpts it flags; design: for a choice that changes contracts, architecture or dependencies, an explorer returns 2-3 short options with trade-offs and the root picks or asks the user, routine choices stay with the writer; debugging: accept a root cause only when reproduction, cause and a fix that makes the reproduction pass close the chain. Keep it short and give the reason for each rule.

(2) Visual trigger: change the root skills section so visual-judging is loaded before the first Worker.visual or Reviewer.visual dispatch (not only at acceptance), and add inline in the acceptance section: say 'round N of 3' in each visual repair brief, at most three rounds per finding, one shared dev server for the visual specialists (dev-server), never open screenshots in the main thread. Extend the dev-server trigger to rendered work served from static or single-file builds, not only a running web app.

(3) Route Reviewer.artifact to Sonnet (keep its effort high), so prose and instruction-text reviews get a stronger reviewer; update every place that states the route (route table, agent frontmatter generation, root routing text that lists Haiku roles, docs).
(4) Point the root's skills section at evidence-judging with its trigger, in one line; keep the always-loaded root text terse.

Follow the holyagent instruction-writing guidance in the repo (packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/skills/instruction-writing if present). Effect/JSDoc rules for any code. Add or update tests that pin the new text, the new skill's presence and the route.
Run node_modules/.bin/mise run build then node_modules/.bin/mise run verify. No version-control writes, no edits under .git/ or .holyagent/; report changed paths.

Keep working until everything asked is done; stop to ask only when you cannot go on. When done and checked, stop and report; name unrequested features instead of adding them. Report in under 400 words; start each evidence line with the criterion label before its colon.
